Beginner Guide: How This Call Trade Works in Plain Dollars

Why this spread works differently from buying shares: TSM pulled back into its major $403.05 support shelf while Pass 1 confirmed COMPOUNDER_PASS fundamentals — even though Stage 2 equity rules wait for trend repair, a defined-risk Bull Call Spread captures a rebound with strictly capped downside.

Exact wallet math (1 contract = 100 shares): You buy the $390 Call for $33.38 and simultaneously sell the $450 Call for $9.65, paying $23.73/sh net ($2,373.00 total for 1 spread(s)). That $2,373.00 is the absolute maximum you can lose.

Breakeven & profit ceiling: At expiry (2027-01-15), you start making money above $413.73 (+3.8% from $398.73). Anywhere at or above $450, your $2,373.00 turns into $6,000.00 (+$3,627.00 net profit).

Speed & time decay in plain English: Today, each $1 move up in TSM adds ~$32.20 to your spread (Net Delta), while sitting flat costs ~$6.62/day in time decay (Net Theta) — much lower than an unhedged call because the sold $450 call decays in your favor.
